place.en: Bhairab Jute Mill · batching department · wage Friday, 4:10 PM

brief.en: The batching muster carries a hundred and forty-one names and the floor can put a face to a hundred and twenty-five. The other sixteen have drawn full wages every fortnight for a year. They have no insurance cards, no nominees, and no hooks worn under their tokens — and every fortnight somebody signs for all sixteen with one thumb.

photoCaption.en: the token board at shift change

iraNote.en: “Sixteen men is a lot of men to never meet. Count the hooks, not the names.”

teaser.en: Sixteen men have drawn a mill’s wages for a year and nobody on the floor has met one of them.

text.en: 141 names. Sixteen of them run unbroken from token 300 to token 315, entered in one hand on one line of the page.
Sixteen thumb impressions against sixteen names. One thumb, sixteen angles — the same whorl every time.
141 hooks. Sixteen of them have never carried brass — the paint under those is unworn.
125 cards issued and numbered. The sixteen have no card, no number and no nominee against any of them.
Sixteen pay envelopes under a rubber band, sealed, dated last fortnight. Fourteen of them still sealed this morning.
Haren Sardar signs out at 5:40 and back in at 6:20. Twice, every wage Friday, for a year.
Eleven men claimed two hours each on the 9th.

text.en: Nine A marks rubbed out and written P, in the mistri’s hand.

text.en: The batching department, last Puja. A hundred and nine faces in the frame.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — nobody counts a mill in a photograph; half the shift was on the machines

text.en: “Numbers above 299 were opened on a written instruction from the office. I keep every instruction. That one is typed and it is not signed.”
“One share in eight stays with me. The other fifteen go back up the stairs in the same envelopes, and I do not put a name to the hand that takes them.”

hook.en: recruits the gang and draws its pay

confession.en: Signed for sixteen men who do not exist, kept one share in eight, and carried the rest back up the stairs every wage Friday at twenty to six.

hook.en: issues every brass token on the board

alibi.en: She opened the numbers on a written office instruction and filed it, which is the opposite of what somebody hiding sixteen men would do.

hook.en: counts out every envelope in the pay office

alibi.en: He pays against the muster the department sends him. A wage clerk who invented sixteen men would have had to invent their insurance cards too, and the cards are simply not there.

hook.en: runs the floor the sixteen are posted to

alibi.en: He has been asking the office for sixteen bodies for a year, in writing, because his floor is short-handed. Nobody complains about the men they are stealing.

hook.en: the muster is passed under his signature

alibi.en: He signs the roll as a total, not as names — and the total has been right to the rupee every fortnight, which is exactly why he never looked at it.

setting.en: The time office, the token board behind her with its hundred and forty-one hooks.

ask.en: How does a man get a token?

answer.en: “He stands in front of me and I give it to him. That is the whole procedure and it has not changed since my father’s time.”

note.en: In front of her. So sixteen men stood here, or the rule bent for sixteen men.

ask.en: Numbers 300 to 315 — who asked for those?

answer.en: “The office. I do not open a new number without a paper.”

note.en: A paper. Every road in this mill ends at a piece of paper somebody upstairs typed.

ask.en: Sixteen hooks on your board have never held brass.

answer.en: “Then those men never took their tokens. The numbers were opened on a written instruction — typed, and not signed. I have kept it.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the token board first. She will not accept a count she has not been shown.

note.en: Typed and unsigned. The second time this mill has produced that exact object.

setting.en: The pay office, behind a grille, envelopes stacked in fifties.

ask.en: Who collects for the batching department?

answer.en: “The sardar, for his gang. That is how it is done everywhere on this bank of the river.”

note.en: Which is true, and is exactly the door this walked through.

ask.en: Sixteen men with no insurance card at all.

answer.en: “Cards are the office’s side, not mine. I pay whoever the muster says, and the muster comes to me signed.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the insurance cards. He will not discuss men you have not proved are missing.

note.en: No card means no nominee, no accident cover, no record anywhere but the wage sheet. They were never meant to survive an audit.

ask.en: Does anybody sign for a whole gang with one thumb?

answer.en: “A sardar puts his own thumb for men who cannot come. For one man, two. Not for sixteen.”

note.en: Not for sixteen. He said it like a man who has been waiting to be asked.

setting.en: The sardar’s room, a tin trunk under the cot, the lid up.

answer.en: “Ramkishun. Ramkishun Yadav.” Then nothing, for a long time.

note.en: One name in a year of Fridays, and he had to reach for it.

ask.en: You go out at twenty to six every wage Friday and come back at twenty past.

answer.en: “A man may take forty minutes for his tea.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the gate pass book. A year of identical Fridays is not a thing to describe — it is a thing to show him.

note.en: Forty minutes, on the one evening a fortnight he is carrying sixteen envelopes.

ask.en: Fourteen of last fortnight’s envelopes are still sealed in your trunk.

answer.en: “One share in eight stays with me. The rest goes back up the stairs, in the same envelopes, and I do not put a name to the hand that takes them.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the bundle from the trunk. Sealed envelopes are the one thing in this room he cannot explain away.

note.en: One in eight. He is not the man who built this — he is the man it pays to carry it.

correction.en: A rubbed-out attendance mark is a kindness. Sixteen names signed with one thumb is a fortnightly wage bill going somewhere — that is the reason.
A group photograph proves nothing about a mill. Sixteen consecutive tokens written onto one line of the muster is a man adding a gang in a single sitting.
An advance against wages is repaid. Fifteen sealed envelopes going back up the stairs every fortnight is where the money actually went.

text.en: The muster says a hundred and forty-one men. The board says which of them ever came to collect brass. Count the worn paint.

bankedClue.en: Sixteen tokens the board never held — and a share in eight, with the rest going back up the stairs
